LESSON: READING 5.2.1 SYNONYMS AND ANTONYMS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we use antonyms and synonyms?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts
2. spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency
3. use synonyms and antonyms in sentences
4. appreciate the importance of correct use of words in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 5.2.1 SYNONYMS AND ANTONYMS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 5.2.1 SYNONYMS AND ANTONYMS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use synonyms and antonyms in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use synonyms and antonyms in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use synonyms and antonyms in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use synonyms and antonyms in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the importance of correct use of words in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of correct use of words in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of correct use of words in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of correct use of words in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms to a partner. (skill: spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: use synonyms and antonyms in sentences)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the importance of correct use of words in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts.
3. Practise this skill: spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency.
4. Practise this skill: use synonyms and antonyms in sentences.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we use antonyms and synonyms?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 5.2.1 Synonyms and Antonyms means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify synonyms and antonyms of words from written texts.
5. Be able to: spell synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
